A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PAC Learning with Improvements. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite appendix reorganization.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F report original classification experiments on Adult, OULAD, Law School and synthetic data, including error curves and numerical model evaluations.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain these original experiments, numerical evaluations and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The learners, neural networks and losses are retained. However, v2 Appendix E.3 removes an undefined outer clipping operation from v1 Appendix F.3's PGD update. Equation 6 already specifies the same radius-r projection in both versions, leaving uncertain whether this is merely a formula correction or a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four binary classification datasets: Adult, OULAD, Law School and the eight-dimensional synthetic dataset. The represented tasks and permitted improvement features are unchanged.

E2.justification: The BCE, weighted-BCE and threshold-based comparisons are retained. The same DTC1, DTC2, RFC1, RFC2 and XGB labeling models participate in the supplementary checks; newly cited related work is not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: The 70/30 splits, preprocessing, model configurations, metrics, classification thresholds and improvement-budget sweeps match. The appendix's deletion of an unspecified outer clipping operation leaves uncertain whether the test-agent simulation procedure changed or only its written expression was corrected.

E4.justification: Both retain the separability analyses, false-positive/false-negative transitions, loss-weight and threshold sweeps, and sensitivity to individual versus agreement-based labeling models. Figures 7–13 introduce no new analysis in v2.

E5.justification: Both specify random seed 42 and retain the same plus/minus uncertainty reporting in Tables 2–3. No additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 2–4 and empirical curves in Figures 3–4 and 6–13 are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains Adult accuracy 0.841087 and OULAD accuracy 0.678003. The rewritten results discussion reports no new outcomes.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects its initial restriction h in H to allow an arbitrary binary hypothesis, aligning it with the existing proper/improper learning distinction. Theorem 3.2 and Example 4 distinguish the restricted hypothesis space from the target concept space more explicitly. The constructions, bounds and proof arguments are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims about zero-error learning, separations from standard and strategic PAC learning, intersection-closed classes, graph learning and empirical benefits of risk aversion.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly identifies a full characterization of proper learning as open, alongside improper learning. Appendix A adds specific prospective extensions to unknown or uncertain improvement sets and learning with tolerance. Existing empirical interpretations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link in the introductory footnote and Section 6. Existing hardware, preprocessing and hyperparameter disclosures remain, including learning rate 0.001 and batch size 64. The linked repository's contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a focused adversarial-robustness discussion with additional citations, contrasting VC-dimension conditions and algorithmic approaches and discussing malicious-noise learning. This extends the existing positioning without replacing the paper's central relationship to strategic classification.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the evaluation introduction and results summary, clarifies concept/hypothesis terminology, adds explicit proof pointers and an Impact Statement, and reorganizes the appendices by moving graph definitions alongside graph proofs. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The same 13 figures and four tables are retained. Figure 4 moves onto the discussion page, Figure 6 moves below the dataset text and Table 1, and several other placements and captions receive small adjustments. The empirical graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility documentation through clearer formal statements, explicit proof pointers, expanded research positioning and a code-access link. The main proofs and empirical evidence remain intact. The ambiguous clipping edit limits conclusions about methodological improvement, but the documented explanatory gains support a small overall improvement.
